Handed to the team · No record of a $50 promise; only the $25 code HD-•••••• is on file.

Different machines, not a better-or-worse thing.

The 40T is raw hashrate: 40 TH/s, BM1370 chips, 650 W, about 16 J/TH. You buy it for the solo odds per dollar.

The B30 is 30 TH/s on the newer BM1373, 485 W flat out, and it drops to 18 TH/s at 230 W in ECO, around 12.8 J/TH. It's the efficient, quiet one if power is expensive where you are.

For maximum chances per dollar, the 40T wins.
I see, so it runs on the new chips wich they run smother, quiet and better on home electricity...

That's the B30, yes. The newer BM1373, quieter at around 50 dB, and much kinder on the meter in ECO mode: 18 TH/s for 230 W.

The 40T has the older BM1370 and pulls 650 W for its 40 TH/s. More hashrate, more power.

So it comes down to what you're optimising. Cheapest odds per dollar, the 40T. Lowest running cost in the house, the B30 at $899.

Which matters more to you, the power bill or the hashrate?

Then the 40T still covers you. It has an Eco mode: 30 TH/s at 450 W, same hashrate as a B30 at full tilt, for $100 less. You can run it in Eco most of the time and open it up when you want.

Two of those at Eco is 60 TH/s for about 900 W, which a normal house circuit handles fine. Heat and noise are the real limits indoors, not the breaker.

Where would they live, a basement or a living space?
small office on the basement

A basement office is about the best spot for them. Both machines sit around 50 dB, roughly a fridge, so a closed door handles it. Two 40Ts at 650 W each is about 1.3 kW of heat, which in a small basement room is real, so leave the door open or run them in Eco in summer. In winter it's free heating.

The trade against the 40T is Bitcoin hashrate: 15 TH/s instead of 40. If Doge matters to you, one of each is a nice pairing.
